observations: Mechanical verification passed: the source excerpt SHA-256, 39652-byte size, canonical core SHA-256, and whole canonical source SHA-256 all matched the assignment metadata.
The window establishes substantial positive constraints for browser packaging, preview trust separation, degraded behavior, shared-buffer mutation, and source-canonical Mermaid rendering.
The candidate findings describe negative space observable within the assigned window only; they do not assert that out-of-range ContractRef documents fail to address the same subjects.

candidate_findings.title: Loopback workspace preview server lacks an enforceable access boundary
candidate_findings.gap: Full HTML/browser mode is rooted to workspace or project context through a localhost server, while its separate trust tier is described only as not inheriting mutation privileges by default. The window does not define listener scope, request authentication, Host or Origin validation, path canonicalization, symlink handling, server lifetime, storage partitioning, or privilege elevation and revocation.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Loopback location is not an authorization boundary. A malicious webpage or local process could probe the server, exploit DNS-rebinding or cross-origin behavior, reach unintended workspace paths, or retain capabilities across a trust-tier transition.
candidate_findings.missing_or_underspecified: The server access-control model; per-session authority; Host, Origin, and CSRF rules; workspace path confinement; cookie and storage isolation; lifecycle shutdown; and the state machine for granting or removing any browser-to-host capability.

evidence_refs.excerpt: - **Full HTML/browser mode** uses a loopback localhost preview server rooted to the workspace/project context.
- Full HTML/browser mode is a **separate trust tier** and must not inherit source-mutation privileges by default.

candidate_findings.title: Generated-preview isolation is policy prose without a concrete enforcement oracle
candidate_findings.gap: The window names a sanitizer and prohibits arbitrary file and network behavior, but it does not define the sanitizer policy, allowed URL schemes, JavaScript boundary, CSP, browser-process enforcement, storage isolation, sanitizer failure outcome, or approval authority for bundled libraries.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Different implementations can all claim compliance while allowing active attributes, unsafe links, network side channels, persistent storage, or unreviewed code. A prose-only network prohibition does not establish where enforcement occurs or how bypasses are detected.
candidate_findings.missing_or_underspecified: Pinned sanitizer configuration and version; allowed tags, attributes, protocols, styles, and SVG behavior; CSP and JavaScript execution rules; network enforcement layer; storage and cookie policy; failure result; conformance corpus; and the principal authorized to approve a bundled library.

evidence_refs.excerpt: - Generated HTML sanitization: `ammonia`

- sanitize generated HTML before it reaches the preview runtime
  - keep JavaScript minimal and preview-runtime-specific
  - do not allow arbitrary file access or arbitrary network behavior as part of the preview contract

- Generated visual modules have an MVP library policy: allowed libraries must be BUNDLED in the source fragment, with no CDN fetches at runtime and no unvetted network requests from within the visual module. The MVP allowlist is empty unless a library is bundled in source, versioned, reviewed, and explicitly approved for that generated visual module; otherwise the agent must inline all code.

candidate_findings.title: Browser runtime lifecycle and health truth are not defined as a state machine
candidate_findings.gap: The window requires atomic replacement, rollback support, runtime health checks, `runtime_unavailable`, and requested/effective disclosure, but it does not define runtime states, transition ordering, health freshness, timeout criteria, crash-loop handling, interrupted-update recovery, concurrent update/use behavior, or the authoritative source of displayed status.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: The GUI can advertise stale or internally inconsistent capability, and update or crash failures can leave the app unable to choose deterministically between the new bundle, the last-known-good bundle, and degraded mode.
candidate_findings.missing_or_underspecified: Installing, validating, active, updating, rollback, damaged, crashed, restarting, degraded, and unavailable states; transition guards; update locking; interruption recovery; health-check timeouts and pass criteria; last-known-good selection; status freshness; and requested/effective projection authority.

candidate_findings.title: User takeover and hidden browser sessions lack control-authority transitions
candidate_findings.gap: The window permits user takeover, watchable background sessions, and hidden auth or testing backends without defining who owns input at each point, how takeover is authorized, whether agent execution pauses, how control is returned, or what privacy indicators and recording rules apply.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Concurrent user and agent input can corrupt transactions or evidence, and hidden authentication sessions can expose credentials or sensitive pages without a clear visibility, consent, or retention boundary.
candidate_findings.missing_or_underspecified: Session owner states; takeover request and acknowledgement; exclusive input arbitration; agent pause, cancellation, and resume semantics; return-of-control transition; access control for watching; hidden-session visibility and consent; credential redaction; and evidence capture rules.

evidence_refs.excerpt: - Browser visibility is watchable by default: normal user-visible browser `/window` sessions let the user `/take` over; attachable background sessions must expose "open live browser session" / "watch run"; hidden utility backends are limited to auth or `/testing/evidence`, not normal user-visible browsing.

candidate_findings.title: Preview mutation has operation fragments but no complete authoritative request envelope
candidate_findings.gap: The operation payloads contain only operation-specific fields, while patch rules depend on `node_id`, `parse_revision`, and `source_revision`, and the outcome set includes `permission_denied`. The window does not bind those values into one request schema or identify document, workspace, caller, capability, request identity, or permission-decision authority.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Requests can be routed to the wrong buffer, replayed after retry, duplicated, or evaluated under the wrong caller authority. Implementations cannot produce interoperable audit records or deterministic permission outcomes.
candidate_findings.missing_or_underspecified: A versioned common envelope containing workspace, document, buffer, node, parse revision, source revision, operation, caller principal, capability, correlation ID, idempotency key, and timestamp; permission evaluation timing and authority; and structured success and error response payloads.

evidence_refs.excerpt:
**Operation payloads**
- `toggle_checkbox` -> `{ target_state?: boolean }`
- `edit_heading_text` -> `{ replacement_text }`
- `edit_list_item_text` -> `{ replacement_text }`
- `set_link_target` -> `{ href, title? }`
- `set_inline_format` -> `{ format: "bold" | "italic" | "code", enable }`
- `replace_mermaid_block` -> `{ replacement_source }`

**Patch rules**
- The runtime MUST resolve `node_id` against the current parse tree for the provided `parse_revision`.
- The runtime MUST validate `source_revision` before patch application.
- The resulting patch MUST stay constrained to the mapped source span for that node or block.
- Requests MUST fail with `ambiguous_mapping` when the requested operation would require modifying text outside the mapped node span.
- Requests MUST fail with `unsupported_region` for raw HTML regions, malformed Markdown regions, unknown extensions, and opaque fenced content.
- Direct preview mutation result codes remain: `applied_patch`, `rejected_stale_revision`, `unsupported_region`, `ambiguous_mapping`, `permission_denied`, `fallback_focus_source`, and `render_error`.

candidate_findings.title: Mutation operations lack content-validation and canonical transformation semantics
candidate_findings.gap: Replacement text, link targets, inline formatting, optional checkbox state, and Mermaid replacement source have no defined size, syntax, escaping, URL-scheme, normalization, or post-transform validation rules. Span confinement alone does not constrain what content is introduced inside the span.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: A bounded patch can still inject structural Markdown, unsafe links, pathological Mermaid, or content that reparses into a different node topology. Different implementations can generate incompatible text for the same logical action.
candidate_findings.missing_or_underspecified: Absent-value semantics for `target_state`; newline and Markdown escaping rules; allowed link schemes and relative-path resolution; title normalization; format nesting behavior; replacement-size limits; Mermaid parse validation before commit; post-patch reparse invariants; and operation-specific test vectors.

candidate_findings.title: Parse mapping and source revision checks lack atomic compare-and-apply semantics

evidence_refs.excerpt:
All successful preview mutations resolve to canonical text patches against the same shared buffer model used by File Editor.
Diff and review flows stay shared-buffer-based: editor review may present side-by-side or `/unified` views; Source Control `/Changes` owns staged, `/unstaged/conflicted`, and conflict states; `/review/rich` preview actions mutate only bounded source spans; annotations remain source-anchored with DOM nodes treated as render projections; and apply-suggestion or one-click edits route through the FileSafe patch `/apply/verify/rollback` path rather than bypassing `/source`, dirty state, or `/redo` history.

**Patch rules**
- The runtime MUST resolve `node_id` against the current parse tree for the provided `parse_revision`.
- The runtime MUST validate `source_revision` before patch application.
- The resulting patch MUST stay constrained to the mapped source span for that node or block.
- Requests MUST fail with `ambiguous_mapping` when the requested operation would require modifying text outside the mapped node span.
- Requests MUST fail with `unsupported_region` for raw HTML regions, malformed Markdown regions, unknown extensions, and opaque fenced content.

**Shared-buffer integration**
- Successful preview edits apply through the same in-memory buffer/update path as File Editor.
- Successful preview edits MUST update dirty state, undo/redo history, and downstream preview re-render using the existing editor/document pipeline.
- Preview actions MUST NOT write directly to disk and MUST NOT bypass the normal save path.
- Each successful preview action creates one undo step unless the host editor later adds explicit coalescing rules.

candidate_findings.title: Patch commit and rerender partial success has no deterministic outcome
candidate_findings.gap: A successful edit is required to update the buffer, dirty state, undo history, and downstream preview, and `applied_patch` says both buffer and preview move to the new revision. The same result set includes `render_error`, but no rule covers a committed buffer patch followed by rerender failure.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: The UI may falsely report failure after committing a change, falsely report success while showing stale content, create duplicate retries, or roll back user text unexpectedly.
candidate_findings.missing_or_underspecified: Commit point; ordering of buffer, undo, dirty-state, and render effects; result precedence when rendering fails after commit; rollback behavior; returned source and render revisions; stale-preview indicator; retry semantics; and audit representation for partial success.

evidence_refs.excerpt:
Selection actions such as `comment`, `replace`, `insert_after`, `remove`, and `send_selection_to_chat` are not direct preview-mutation operations.

- On source-backed or deterministically mapped preview surfaces, selection actions may create durable annotations or `document_selection_context` attachments.

- Chat and planning surfaces may issue non-destructive selection handoff only until they are explicitly wired to the validated mutation path.
- Audit must distinguish `created_annotation`, `selection_sent_to_chat`, and `selection_forward_blocked` from direct patch outcomes.
